newsitem.title: GERMANY: German stocks seen continuing consolidation.
newsitem.headline: German stocks seen continuing consolidation.

text.p: German shares were expected to continue to consolidate and could attempt to breach the 2,700 level in the coming days, traders said on Monday.
The IBIS Dax, which reflects all-day computer dealings in the DAX, was up 3.46 points at 2,696.15, while the DAX ended floor trade up 7.85 at 2,693.88.
The market was encouraged by strength on Wall Street although the U.S. Columbus day holiday kept volumes light.
Although some analysts said the DAX was consolidating at these levels, others said the index could have to correct down to 2,650, before making further substantial advances.
Analysts at Trinkaus and Burkhardt said several factors could lead to an extended period of consolidation. First, they said, the advance on the German bond market was petering out.
Secondly, they see stocks as being technically overbought. Finally the imminent flotation of Deutsche Telekom is making some investors hesitant.
But most analysts were bullish for the longer term, with year-end targets around 2,750.
They said U.S. September consumer price data would provide direction for the week.
